{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=January 2013}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |mode=Basketball |year=2009–10 |team=Clemson Tigers |image=Clemson Tigers logo.svg |image_size=125 |conference=Atlantic Coast Conference |division= |short_conf=ACC |CoachRank= |APRank= |record=21–11 |conf_record=9–7 |head_coach=[[Oliver Purnell]] |hc_year=7th |asst_coach1=[[Ron Bradley]] |asst_coach2=Frank Smith |asst_coach3=Josh Postorino |stadium=[[Littlejohn Coliseum]] |champion= |bowl=[[2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result=First Round }} {{2009–10 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2009–10 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team''' represented [[Clemson University]] in the [[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10]] [[college basketball]] season. Their head coach was [[Oliver Purnell]]. The team played its home games at [[Littlejohn Coliseum]] in [[Clemson, SC|Clemson]], [[South Carolina]] and are members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. All games were produced and [[Radio broadcasting|broadcast locally]] by the [[Clemson Tigers Sports Network]]. The Tigers finished the season 21–11, 9–7 in ACC play. They lost in the first round of the [[2010 ACC men's basketball tournament]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]], earning a 7 seed in the East Region, where they lost to [[2009–10 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]] in the first round. == Pre-season == On Wednesday, May 27, guard [[Terrence Oglesby]] announced he would forgo his final two seasons at the school to pursue a professional basketball career. Oglesby appeared in 66 games and scored 777 points in his two seasons at Clemson. Previously, Oglesby played for [[Norway]] at the [[International Basketball Federation]] (FIBA) [[FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]]. In a press release issued by Clemson University, Oglesby indicated that his time spent playing internationally helped fuel his decision to turn pro.{{cite web | url=http://clemsontigers.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/052709aaa.html | work=Men's Basketball | publisher=ClemsonTigers.com | title=Oglesby to Leave Clemson to Pursue Professional Basketball Career | accessdate=2009-05-27 | archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20090610075936/http://clemsontigers.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/052709aaa.html| archivedate= June 10, 2009 | url-status= live}} Oglesby's departure left an open roster spot which was filled by the commitment of shooting guard Noel Johnson, a former [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] commitment.[http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/news?slug=ap-clemson-johnson&prov=ap&type=lgns Johnson turns to Clemson after Floyd leaves USC] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090721000406/http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/news?slug=ap-clemson-johnson&prov=ap&type=lgns |date=July 21, 2009 }} On Tuesday, August 18, [[ESPN]] announced that Clemson will serve as one of the host sites for the network's popular basketball series, [[College GameDay (basketball)|College GameDay]], during the [[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Two one-hour shows (11:00 am and 8:00 pm Eastern) will originate from [[Littlejohn Coliseum]] on Jan 23, 2010 for the Clemson vs. [[2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] game. This is Clemson's first appearance on ESPN College GameDay. The series, which is in its sixth season, will make four first-time stops in 2010. Other first-time hosts include Illinois, Kansas State and Washington. The Clemson/Duke game will be one of two ACC tilts featured this season, with the other being North Carolina at Duke on Mar. 6.{{cite web | url=http://clemson.scout.com/2/889607.html | work=CUTigers | publisher=Scout.com | title=Gameday coming to Clemson | accessdate=2009-08-18 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716021322/http://clemson.scout.com/2/889607.html | archive-date=July 16, 2011 | url-status=dead }} On Sunday, October 26, 2008, members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] Media were polled and picked Clemson to finish third in the conference behind North Carolina and Duke.{{cite web | url=http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102509aab.html | work=Men's Basketball | publisher=The ACC | title=Media Splits Top Spot in 2009–10 ACC Preseason Poll | accessdate=2008-10-25 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120308100008/http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102509aab.html | archive-date=March 8, 2012 | url-status=dead }} == Regular season == On December 2, 2009, [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] came back from a 23-point second-half deficit to upset the No. 18 Tigers, 76–74 at Littlejohn Coliseum. The victory was the biggest comeback win in school history and was also notable as it helped the [[Big Ten]] win their first [[ACC – Big Ten Challenge]] in eleven tries.[http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/34248575/ns/sports-college_basketball/ Illinois’ monster 2nd half stuns No. 18 Clemson] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100105182903/http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/34248575/ns/sports-college_basketball/ |date=January 5, 2010 }} On December 6, 2009, Clemson beat rival South Carolina 72–61, extending their winning streak over the Gamecocks to six games. Carolina leads the overall series, 86–74. On January 3, 2010, the No. 21 Tigers managed only 12 points in the first half as they lost to No. 7 [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] for the 13th straight time at [[Cameron Indoor Stadium]], 74–53. Clemson had as many fouls as points in the opening period, and their scoring total and shooting percentage (5–30, 17%) were the lowest for a half in Oliver Purnell's seven years as head coach.[https://web.archive.org/web/20100109181756/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300030150 Duke holds No. 18 Clemson to 12 first-half points in blowout win] On January 13, 2010, the No. 19 Tigers ended a 10-game losing streak to North Carolina by defeating the No. 13 Tar Heels, 83–64 at Littlejohn Arena. It was the second largest margin of victory ever for the Tigers over the Tar Heels. The most being a 20-point 93–73 win in 1976–77, [[Tree Rollins]]' senior season.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120318054745/http://clemsontigers.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/011410aam.html|title=Clemson vs. North Carolina Postgame Notes}} Clemson then followed the win with a 73–70 win at NC State, ending a streak of 13 consecutive losses in the game following a victory over a top 25 team.[http://clemsontigers.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/011610aaa.html Tigers Top North Carolina State, 73–70] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100121161026/http://clemsontigers.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/011610aaa.html |date=January 21, 2010 }} [[File:2010 College Gameday at Clemson.jpg|right|thumb|College GameDay live broadcast from Littlejohn Coliseum (Jan 23, 2010)]]On January 23, 2010, [[ESPN]]'s [[College GameDay (basketball)|College GameDay]] broadcast live from [[Littlejohn Coliseum]] for the first time. Afterward, GameDay host [[Digger Phelps]] said of the broadcast at Clemson: "It was the best". The crowd was so loud during the broadcast that the production director requested that the crowd keep the noise down when cameras were rolling.[http://clemson.scout.com/a.z?s=46&p=2&c=940271 Duke Dominates PHELPS: "It was the best"] The day culminated in a 60–47 loss to Duke, the lowest point total for Duke thus far this season, and the lowest point total of a Clemson team at home since the 2003–04 season, Oliver Purnell's first at Clemson.[http://ncaabasketball.fanhouse.com/2010/01/24/duke-routs-clemson/ Duke Dominates With Defense, Routs Clemson] == Postseason == === ACC tournament === Clemson entered the [[2010 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] as the No. 6 seed with a 9–7 record in the ACC regular season. The Tigers lost their opening game to No. 11 seed NC State 59–57, dropping their record in the tournament to 16–57 all-time with 43 of their losses coming in the first round. Clemson remains the only original member of the ACC to have never won the tournament.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120730131218/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300700228|title=North Carolina State drops Clemson from ACC tourney}} === NCAA tournament === Clemson entered the tournament as the No. 7 seed in the East Region, but was knocked out in the opening round by a lower-seeded team for the third straight year, losing 86–78 to No. 10 seed Missouri. The loss dropped Oliver Purnell to 0–6 all-time in NCAA Tournament games as a head coach for three different schools.[http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recap?gid=201003190120 Missouri stifles Booker, beats Clemson 86–78] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100323063205/http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recap?gid=201003190120 |date=March 23, 2010 }} == Roster == ===
